summary.text: 告 is commonly used to tell, report, announce, inform, and accuse. Its early construction is disputed: proposals read it as a mouth with a protruding tongue, as 口 with 牛, or as 口 with an abbreviated 壴.

formation.text: The competing analyses treat 告 either as a picture of an open mouth with a tongue projecting upward from it, or as a compound of 口 and an upper element identified as 牛 or abbreviated 壴. The latter proposal allows 壴 to be phonetic, but its role is uncertain; no sound component is securely identified across the analyses.

components.text: In the tongue proposal, 口 depicts an open mouth and the upward stroke is understood as a protruding tongue. In the alternative accounts it is paired with 牛 or 壴; those accounts do not establish a separate function for 口.

history.text: The received Shuowen explanation pictures an ox striking a person while a crossbar restrains its horns, thereby informing people, and analyzes 告 as 牛 plus 口. This is a historical explanation, not confirmation of the construction of the earlier graph.

A later graphic account describes the seal form as abbreviated in clerical writing and regularized into the modern shape. The curated seal image represents the Shuowen tradition; it does not settle the competing analyses of earlier forms.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s upper element remains disputed: it has been analyzed as a tongue-related stroke, 牛, or an abbreviated 壴. The 壴 proposal comes from an article abstract, and its proposed function is uncertain.

A Southwestern Mandarin word meaning “try” or “check out” is proposed to have been written with 告 by borrowing the graph for 校. Similar Middle Chinese readings are reported, but the borrowing direction and sound pathway remain uncertain.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and later examples reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: A reported oracle-bone example concerns a deer report, and later examples use 告 for reporting or telling. These attest the meanings but do not establish a single original meaning or a sequence of semantic change.

senses.period: Western Zhou examples reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Western Zhou bronze examples include reporting and admonishing uses. Their chronology and development from earlier senses are not established.

senses.period: Western Zhou examples reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Accusatory use is reported among Western Zhou bronze examples; its relationship to “report” is not established.
Current uses include telling, announcing, informing, and accusing. The available glosses do not establish their chronology or semantic connections.

A Southwestern Mandarin word meaning “try” or “check out” is attested in a 1909 example. The proposed account is that 告 borrowed the graph for 校 to write this similar-sounding word, rather than developing this meaning from “tell”; the borrowing direction and sound pathway remain uncertain.

limitations.text: The cited examples do not establish a sequence connecting sacrificial, reporting, admonishing, accusatory, and telling uses.
The proposed borrowing from 校 lacks independent confirmation of its source account and historical sound pathway; similarity alone does not establish the borrowing direction.

overview.text: 告 is commonly used to tell and report. Its early construction is disputed: one proposal sees an open mouth with a protruding tongue; others pair 口 with 牛 or abbreviated 壴.

components.text: In one proposal, 口 depicts an open mouth; other analyses pair it with 牛 or 壴.

relationships.text: In the protruding-tongue proposal, 口 depicts the open mouth; alternative analyses also place 口 in a 牛-plus-mouth or 壴-plus-mouth construction without specifying its separate function.
